subject: Maths
title: Solving by elimination
subtitle: Simultaneous Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve simultaneous linear equations by adding or subtracting to eliminate a variable.

key_vocab.definition: The elimination method removes one variable by adding or subtracting the equations. We make the coefficients of one variable equal (by multiplying), then add or subtract.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve simultaneous linear equations by adding or subtracting to eliminate a variable.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: elimination method -- The elimination method removes one variable by adding or subtracting the equations. We make the coefficients of one variable equal (by multiplying), then add or subtract.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Make coefficients of one variable equal, then add (if different signs) or subtract (if same signs) to eliminate it.
2x + 3y = 12 and 2x − y = 4: subtract ⇒ 4y = 8
Same coefficient of x (both 2x): subtract equations

Key examples:
  ✓ 2x + y = 7 and x + y = 4: subtract to get x = 3  (same sign y, subtract)
  ✓ 3x + 2y = 12 and 3x − y = 3: subtract to eliminate x  (same coefficient of x)
  ✓ May need to multiply one or both equations first  (to match coefficients)
  ✗ Always add the equations  (sometimes subtract)
  ✗ Coefficients must already match  (multiply to make them match)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – simple subtraction
  Solve 2x + y = 7 and x + y = 4
  Subtract equation 2 from equation 1: (2x+y) − (x+y) = 7 − 4
  x = 3
  Substitute: 3 + y = 4, so y = 1
  x = 3, y = 1
  (Both equations have +y, so subtract to eliminate y.)

Example 2 – simple addition
  Solve 3x + 2y = 16 and x − 2y = 0
  Add the equations: (3x+2y) + (x−2y) = 16 + 0
  4x = 16, so x = 4
  Substitute: 4 − 2y = 0, so y = 2
  x = 4, y = 2
  (+2y and −2y: add to eliminate y.)

sections.title: Direct elimination
sections.content:
Solve by adding or subtracting directly.

(a) x + y = 6 and x − y = 2
(b) 2x + y = 9 and 2x − y = 1
(c) 3x + 2y = 14 and x + 2y = 10
(d) 5x + y = 17 and 3x + y = 11

sections.title: Multiply one equation
sections.content:
Multiply one equation first, then eliminate.

(a) 2x + y = 8 and x + 3y = 9
(b) 3x + 2y = 16 and x + y = 6
(c) 4x + y = 14 and 2x + 3y = 12
(d) x + 2y = 7 and 3x + y = 11

sections.title: Multiply both equations
sections.content:
Multiply both equations to match a coefficient.

(a) 2x + 3y = 13 and 3x + 2y = 12
(b) 3x + 4y = 18 and 5x + 2y = 16
(c) 4x + 3y = 23 and 3x + 5y = 24
(d) 2x + 5y = 19 and 3x + 4y = 18

sections.title: Negative coefficients
sections.content:
Solve each pair.

(a) 2x − y = 5 and x + y = 7
(b) 3x − 2y = 5 and x + 2y = 7
(c) 4x − 3y = 1 and 2x + 3y = 17
(d) 5x − y = 13 and 2x + 3y = 12

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each pair of simultaneous equations.

(a) x + y = 8 and 2x + 3y = 21
(b) 3x + 2y = 19 and x − y = 2
(c) 4x + y = 10 and x + 4y = 10
(d) 2x + 5y = 1 and 3x − 2y = −12
(e) x + 2y = 10 and 3x − y = 9

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Same signs: subtract equations. Different signs: add equations
✗ You can only use elimination if coefficients already match
✓ After finding one variable, substitute back to find the other
✗ Always add the equations together
✓ You can multiply one or both equations to create matching coefficients

  (b) x = 4, y = 2

  (b) x = 2, y = 3
